findings.title: 'replicates on X only (hardware-conditional)' is issued without any block x policy interaction test, and at the historical baseline rates it is the most likely label even when the gain is the same on both GPU models
findings.evidence: classify() labels a result 'hardware-conditional' whenever the H10 clause holds in exactly one block. No test checks whether the two blocks' effects differ. Computed with analysis.fisher_one_sided (scratchpad protocol-stats/power.py, power2.py), assuming independent blocks. (1) Same rates on both models (p0=0.234, p1=0.45): per-block power 0.360, P(label says hardware-conditional)=0.461. At p1=0.5625 it is 0.438. (2) Same candidate rate, but each baseline at its v5-v8 per-model H10 history (RTX 8000 3/24 = 0.125, all at dev06; A40 12/40 = 0.30): at p1=0.45 the power is 0.736 on RTX and 0.196 on A40, so P('replicates on rtx8000 only')=0.592. At p1=0.35 it is 0.442 and at p1=0.54 it is 0.523. (3) Concrete pairs that get the label: 8/24 vs 2/24 (p=0.036, passes) with 7/24 vs 3/24 (p=0.143, fails); 7/24 vs 1/24 with 6/24 vs 2/24. For both, Zelen's exact homogeneity p=1.000 and the Wald difference-of-differences p is about 0.57-0.60. For context, multiplicity itself is small: the per-block clause's real size is about 2.6% at n=24 (Fisher is conservative), so P(at least 1 of 2 blocks passes under the null) is about 5.2%. The problem is the interaction inference, not Bonferroni.
findings.failure_scenario: The candidate's true H10 rate does not depend on the GPU. The RTX block passes, because its baseline sits near 3/24, and the A40 block misses by one or two episodes. results.json and STATUS.md then record 'replicates on rtx8000 only (hardware-conditional)', a hardware claim the data cannot support. The stop rule blocks any change to that label after launch.
findings.fix: Before freezing, preregister an interaction test. Options: Zelen's exact conditional test of equal odds ratios over the two blocks' 2x2 tables, or, since the rows are shared, an exact sign-flip over the 8 rows of (cand-base margin on rtx8000) minus (cand-base margin on a40). Emit 'hardware-conditional' only when that test gives p < 0.05. Otherwise emit 'H10 clause holds on X, not on Y; block x policy interaction not established (p=...)'. Add one README sentence: the design cannot separate the candidate's hardware sensitivity from the baseline's (RTX H10 3/24 vs A40 12/40 historically). Name cross_block as the descriptive tool for that question. Record the multiplicity figure (about 5.2% familywise for 'passes somewhere') in the protocol.

findings.title: No preregistered power, so 'does not replicate' will read as a negative result; the approved A40 block has 6-42% power
findings.where: manifest protocol (scripts/build_manifest.py:221-260), README.md:47-61, scripts/analysis.py:325-326 and 350-367 (combined test)
findings.evidence: v8's manifest preregistered 'confirmatory_power'. v9's protocol has no power statement at all. Per-block H10 clause power on 24 vs 24: at pooled p0=0.234 it is 0.142, 0.360 and 0.676 for p1 = 0.35, 0.45 and 0.5625. At the A40 baseline's history (p0=0.30) it is 0.057, 0.196 and 0.418 for p1 = 0.35, 0.45 and 0.54. With p0=0.234 and p1=0.45, P(neither block passes) = 0.410. The combined 48 vs 48 Fisher has power 0.664 in the same scenario, and P(neither block passes AND pooled 48 vs 48 p<0.05) = 0.126. So in about 1 run in 8, 'does not replicate' would sit beside a significant combined test, and the protocol does not say which one governs. It only lists the block x pose test as 'secondary_reported_not_gated'. The minimum candidate count to pass is 5/24 against 0, 8 against 2, 9 against 3, 11 against 4 and 14 against 7. The margin >= 4 clause never binds, because p < 0.05 already forces a margin of at least 5.
findings.failure_scenario: an1 truly raises H10 from about 0.30 to 0.45 on A40. The approved A40 block fails the clause about 80% of the time and reports 'does not replicate'. Readers take that as evidence against the gain, even when the pooled 48 vs 48 test is significant.
findings.fix: Add protocol.power with a per-model table (RTX p0 about 0.125, A40 p0 about 0.30; p1 = 0.35, 0.45, 0.54). Rename the negative label to 'not replicated (power X-Y%)'. Decide now whether the block x pose stratified 48 vs 48 test is primary, or state that it cannot override the per-block reading. Note that at 24 vs 24 the binding threshold is p < 0.05, which requires a margin of at least 5 to 7.

findings.title: 'partially measured' holds a complete block's reading hostage to the other block; the user approved an A40-only design, and A40 completion before the deadline is uncertain
findings.evidence: classify() returns 'partially measured' whenever len(measured) < len(blocks), whatever the complete block shows. The approved step was A40-only: 96 episodes with --constraint=a40. sinfo now: cn-r-1/2 draining, cn-r-3..6, cn-s-1..3 and cn-gpu5 drained. Reservation root_204 (2026-10-01 08:00-16:00, MAINT) covers cn-gpu[5-7], cn-r-[1-6], cn-s-[1-5] and cn-t-1. The deadline is 2026-10-06. There is no preregistered reading for a single complete block. Nothing in the protocol forbids or records a manual scancel of a queued block after the other block's result appears in STATUS.md (driver.record_block writes per-block H10/H50 and p as soon as that block ends).
findings.failure_scenario: The RTX block completes on about 09-29 and the A40 block misses 10-06. The campaign reports 'partially measured', and the author decides after seeing the data how to read the RTX result. Or, after seeing the RTX result, someone cancels the A40 array, and no rule records that as a deviation.
findings.fix: Preregister that each complete block's H10 and H50 clause results are readings in their own right: A40 is the approved primary, RTX 8000 is replication on a second model. Restrict 'partially measured' to the cross-model classification. Add to the stop rule: 'no manual cancellation of a block; any cancellation other than the deadline is reported as a protocol deviation'.

findings.title: The second half of the stated question (does an1's dev01 H50 loss survive?) has no preregistered decision rule
findings.evidence: The question reads: 'Do an1's H10 gain ... and its dev01 H50 loss survive fresh seeds'. The only dev01 output is hb['p_b_settled'], raw per-block counts over 3 vs 3 episodes, listed as 'reported, not gated'. The classification covers only the H10 gain. History is GPU-dependent: baseline dev01 H50 was 4/4 on A40 and 1/4 on RTX 8000 over v5-v8; an1 was 0/2, both on A40 (my tabulation, scratchpad history_rows.json).
findings.failure_scenario: On RTX the baseline also fails dev01 H50, say 0/3 vs 0/3, while on A40 it is 3/3 vs 0/3. With no rule, the author decides after seeing the data whether the loss 'survived', 'is A40-only' or 'is inconclusive'.
findings.fix: Either preregister a rule now, for example 'the dev01 H50 loss replicates in a complete block iff baseline dev01 H50 settled > candidate; reported per block and pooled; 3 vs 3 per block is descriptive and cannot reach significance', or remove dev01 from the question and list it only as descriptive.

findings.title: 'The two blocks ... measure the GPU effect directly' is inaccurate: shared seeds give no pairing across models, and the blocks are confounded with date, node set, driver and kernel, none of which the analysis records
findings.evidence: v8 REPORT finding 5: episodes on different GPU models 'differ from action 1 (0 of 219 H10 pairs share an action)'. Sharing seeds across blocks therefore adds no variance reduction, and cross_block is an unpaired 48 vs 48. The blocks will run on different days, and very likely on opposite sides of the 2026-10-01 all-GPU maintenance (root_204). The v8 rollout.log device table shows 'Driver Version: 595.71.05' (line 38) and kernel 5.14.0-611.55.1.el9_7. The login node already runs 5.14.0-687.52.1.el9_8. episode() extracts only the GPU name. Driver version, kernel and hostname are neither parsed nor reported.
findings.failure_scenario: The A40 block runs after a driver or kernel upgrade during maintenance. cross_block and the classification attribute the between-block difference to 'GPU model' even though the driver, date and node pool changed too.
findings.fix: In episode(), also parse 'Driver Version', the kernel line and the hostname (or read NodeList from sacct), and report them per block in block_results. Rewrite README:40-41 and why_two_blocks to say it is an unpaired comparison of two blocks, confounded with node set, date and software stack unless those match. Soften any GPU-model attribution in the report if the driver or kernel differ between blocks.

findings.title: 'pose_stratified_exact_p' and 'pose_sign_flip_p' are row-stratified (8 dev slots), not pose-stratified in v8's sense, and the 3-cluster test v8 reported is not computed
findings.evidence: The strata are keyed by development_pose_slot (8 rows). tests/test_v9.py:99-100 assert 0.012 and 0.047, which are v8 REPORT's 'by row p = 0.012' and 'rows as the unit 0.047'. v8 REPORT separately reports 'by pose 0.011', the P_A/P_B/P_C clusters. The approved next step said 'row-stratified and row sign-flip tests'. CLAUDE.md warns that pose-grouping errors have already produced a wrong claim once.
findings.failure_scenario: The v9 report sets 'pose-stratified p' beside v8's 'by pose 0.011' and compares two different tests.
findings.fix: Rename the fields and docs to row_stratified_exact_p and row_sign_flip_p. Optionally add a cluster-stratified test using cluster_of().

findings.title: The retry scope in the docs is narrower than the code: tasks that produced a rollout but failed validation are also re-drawn
findings.where: README.md:75-76; manifest protocol.stop_rule; scripts/driver.py:265-276 and 320-333; scripts/run_matched_task.py:265-283
findings.evidence: The README says 'one retry only for tasks that left no completed rollout'. driver.read_result returns None for any status other than 'completed'. That includes validate_result failures such as 'non-finite simulator state' and checker/terminal disagreement, where rollout.json exists. Those outputs are moved to attempts/ and re-run. Such failures can depend on the policy. Historical rate across v5-v8 matched evaluations: 0 of 376 (every status.json reads 'completed'; no attempts/ directories).
findings.failure_scenario: The candidate's aggressive grasp drives the physics non-finite. The episode is retried rather than counted as a failure, which shifts the count toward the policy that destabilises the simulation.
findings.fix: Document exactly which states trigger a retry, and record the retried directories with their states in the block results. Or treat 'non-finite simulator state' as a policy outcome (invalid for both arms of that row) rather than as infrastructure.

findings.title: Secondary p-values are unadjusted, and for incomplete blocks the reported counts and the paired tests use different denominators
findings.evidence: Each block and horizon reports Fisher, row-stratified, sign-flip and McNemar tests, plus the combined test, with no multiplicity statement. cs, cn, bs and bn count every valid episode per arm, while strata, diffs and McNemar use only rows where both arms are valid. The two sets diverge only in incomplete blocks, which are descriptive.
findings.failure_scenario: An incomplete block shows 'candidate 7/23' next to a stratified p computed on 22 pairs. A reader takes them as the same sample.
findings.fix: Add a protocol sentence that secondary p-values are unadjusted and descriptive. In block_results, report n_paired beside the paired tests, or compute the headline counts on paired rows when a block is incomplete.

checked_ok: fisher_one_sided matches scipy.stats.fisher_exact(alternative='greater'): max |diff| 3.3e-16 over 3000 random tables (n up to 30 per arm).

stratified_exact matches brute-force enumeration of per-stratum hypergeometrics: max |diff| 1.0e-15 over 300 random strata sets. It also matches a 200k-rep Monte Carlo permutation under fixed stratum margins (0.02278 vs 0.02331; 0.05055 vs 0.05022, within about 1.6 MC SE). With a single stratum it equals Fisher exactly.
sign_flip equals itertools enumeration exactly (500 random vectors of length 1-9). mcnemar_exact equals scipy.stats.binomtest(greater) (max |diff| 2.2e-16 over 0..24 x 0..24).

The per-block primary equals v8 matched_verdict (v8 scripts/driver.py:107-130). It uses the same Fisher formula (the test asserts equality with v8's function), margin >= 4, p < 0.05, H50 cand >= base and settled = terminal_success. 'complete' requires 48 valid rows per policy (96 episodes). analysis.episode also invalidates any episode whose status or log GPU differs from the block's pinned model (analysis.py:207-208), which is stricter than v8.
At 24 vs 24 the margin >= 4 clause never binds: p < 0.05 already requires cand - base >= 5 (minimum candidate count 5, 6, 8, 9 and 11 for baseline 0 to 4).

Seed freshness: rg over every non-binary file in the repo (runtime logs, request.json, ledgers, plans, media indexes) found 97000-97207 only in v9's own files. The other hits were PNG IDAT byte counts in isaaclab logs, a hex digest '97201f45...' and a media byte count 97207. There were no hits in lehome-data/outputs. The runner seeds the python, numpy, torch, cuda and garment RNGs directly from --seed (policy_rollout51.py:328-331, 486-488).

Seed sharing matches the description: each of the 24 (pose, seed_block) cells has exactly one seed, used by both the H10 and H50 rows. Both policies share a row through the index // 2 interleave, and both blocks read the same manifest rows.

rid[3:5] == development_pose_slot on all 48 rows, so compute() and block_results group identically. cluster_of maps P_A to dev00/04/06, P_B to dev01/03 and P_C to dev02/05/07 by match_pose, matching CLAUDE.md.

NaN or None margins: 0 of 256 valid v5-v8 episodes. The runner float()s all four condition margins (policy_rollout51.py:1426), and geometric_ever_success is present in all 256, so results JSON will not contain NaN.

Multiplicity of 'passes on at least one model': the per-block clause's real size is about 2.6% (p0 = 0.2 to 0.3), so the familywise rate is about 5.2%. This is near nominal and belongs as a statement (see PS-1), not a correction.
tests/test_v9.py: 13 passed on the login node.

verdicts.reason: Reproduced independently (scratchpad protocol-stats-verify/power.py, combined.py). classify() (analysis.py:319-326) issues 'replicates on X only (hardware-conditional)' whenever exactly one complete block passes, and no interaction test is run. Numbers: with the same rates on both models (p0=0.234, p1=0.45), per-block power is 0.360 and P(exactly one block passes) is 0.461; at p1=0.5625 it is 0.438. With per-model baselines (RTX 0.125, A40 0.30), P('rtx8000 only') is 0.442, 0.592 and 0.523 at p1 = 0.35, 0.45 and 0.54. The concrete pairs check out: 8/24 vs 2/24 (p=0.0361, passes) against 7/24 vs 3/24 (p=0.1432, fails) gives Zelen p=1.000 and Wald difference-of-differences p=0.603. 7/24 vs 1/24 (p=0.0240) against 6/24 vs 2/24 (p=0.1224) gives Zelen 1.000 and Wald 0.568. The null size per block is 0.019-0.030, so the familywise rate is about 5.2%. One caveat: scenario (2) is not a false label, because the risk-difference gain really does differ by model when the baselines differ. The clean false-positive case is scenario (1), P about 0.46, which is enough on its own to rate this major.
verdicts.fix_after: Replace the '(hardware-conditional)' label with 'H10 clause holds on <X>, not on <Y>'. Preregister an interaction test and name its scale: Zelen's exact test on the two blocks' 2x2 tables (odds ratio), or an exact sign-flip over the 8 shared rows of (cand-base margin on rtx8000) minus (cand-base margin on a40) (risk difference). Claim hardware dependence only if that test gives p<0.05. State in the protocol that at 24 per arm per block the test is nearly powerless, so 'interaction not established' cannot be read as 'no hardware effect'. Also state that a model-dependent gain can come from the baseline's own hardware sensitivity (RTX H10 3/24 vs A40 12/40 historically), not the candidate's. Record the ~5.2% familywise rate for 'passes in at least one block'. Add tests for the 'exactly one' and 'neither' branches.

verdicts.reason: Reproduced exactly. v8's manifest has protocol.confirmatory_power; v9's manifest and README contain no power statement (grep -i power on the v9 manifest returns nothing). Per-block power at p0=0.234 is 0.142, 0.360 and 0.676 for p1 = 0.35, 0.45 and 0.5625. At A40 p0=0.30 it is 0.057, 0.196 and 0.418 for p1 = 0.35, 0.45 and 0.54. With p0=0.234 and p1=0.45, P(neither block passes) is 0.410. The pooled 48 vs 48 Fisher has power 0.664, and P(neither passes AND pooled p<0.05) is 0.126. With the code's actual block x row stratified test (Monte Carlo, 20k draws) the figures are 0.651 and 0.124. Minimum passing counts at 24 vs 24: 5, 6, 8, 9 and 11 against 0-4, and 14 against 7. Margin >= 4 never binds (the minimum margin with p<0.05 is 5). One sub-claim is overstated: 'the protocol does not say which one governs'. Listing the combined test under secondary_reported_not_gated already implies it does not govern. The power gap stands without that sub-claim.
verdicts.fix_after: Add protocol.power with a per-model table. Use preregistered p1 values (0.35, 0.45, 0.54) and per-model p0 taken from the v5-v8 history (RTX 3/24 = 0.125, A40 12/40 = 0.30, pooled 15/64 = 0.234), so the quoted range is not chosen after the fact. Rename the negative label to 'not replicated at this power (A40 x%, RTX y%)'. State explicitly that the block x row combined test is descriptive and cannot override the per-block readings. Note that at 24 vs 24 the binding threshold is p<0.05, which needs a margin of at least 5, and that margin >= 4 is vestigial.

verdicts.reason: Overstated. protocol.per_block_primary already gives each block its own preregistered reading. For a partial result, classify() still emits h10_clause_holds_on and v5_rule_holds_on for the complete block, and record_block writes the full per-block result. So nothing is held hostage; only the headline label reads 'partially measured'. The cluster facts are correct: cn-r-1/2 are draining, cn-r-3..6, cn-s-1..5, cn-t-1 and cn-gpu5 are drained (maint), and root_204 (2026-10-01 08:00-16:00) covers all of them. But about 96 x ~4 min / 8 GPUs is about an hour of work, and there are ~4 days between that maintenance and the 10-06 deadline, so non-completion is plausible, not likely. The manual-scancel point is wrong as stated. A manually cancelled block is not left unrecorded: sacct CANCELLED goes to summarize() as 'failed', and block_stage (driver.py:314-333) then auto-resubmits every unfinished task as the block's single retry and logs 'one outcome-blind retry of N tasks without a completed rollout'. So the cancellation would be mislabeled as a task failure, not left unrecorded.
verdicts.fix_after: When exactly one block is complete, have classify() emit '<block> measured: H10 clause holds/fails; cross-model classification not available (<other> incomplete)'. Name A40 as the approved primary block in the protocol (see missed item 1). In block_stage, compare sacct CANCELLED states against the driver's own deadline cancellations, and log an external cancellation as a protocol deviation rather than a retry. Add to the stop rule that any cancellation other than the deadline is reported as a deviation.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. The README (lines 11-13) and manifest 'question' both ask whether 'its dev01 H50 loss' survives, but the only dev01 output is the descriptive hb['p_b_settled'] (analysis.py:301-303), 3 vs 3 per block. No rule states what counts as the loss surviving. My independent tabulation of v5-v8 (history.py) shows this exact cell split by GPU model for the baseline: dev01 H50 is A40 4/4 and RTX 8000 1/4, and an1's 0/2 was entirely on A40. The per-block readings will therefore probably diverge, which leaves a headline question open to a post-hoc story. At 3 vs 3 a block cannot reach p<0.05 (0/3 vs 3/3 gives p=0.05 exactly), so any rule has to be descriptive, but it still has to be written down before launch.
verdicts.fix_after: Either preregister a descriptive rule, for example 'the dev01 H50 loss recurs in a complete block iff baseline dev01 H50 settled > candidate; reported per block and pooled over 6 vs 6 (one-sided Fisher reported, not gated); 3 vs 3 per block cannot reach significance', or remove dev01 from the question and keep it only under secondary_reported_not_gated.

verdicts.reason: Primary evidence contradicts the failure scenario. I compared exact executed_action_rad prefixes from rollout.json.behavior.jsonl over every v5-v8 same-policy, same-row, same-seed pair (driver_prefix.py). There are 58 same-model pairs on different drivers (595.71.05/el9_7 vs 615.71.09/el9_8; 34 A40 episodes ran on 615, including v8's three on cn-s-2). They share action prefixes with the same distribution as same-driver pairs: median 70 actions at H10 and 100 at H50, and no pair has a zero-length prefix. All 254 cross-model pairs diverge at action 1. So the driver and kernel are not quasi-seeds, and 'the A40 block runs after a maintenance upgrade' is not a confound. Date has no mechanism in a code-pinned simulation. Two small points survive. (a) The node platform varies with the GPU model and cannot be separated from it here: sinfo features show the A40 nodes are epyc/AVX2 and the RTX nodes cascadelake/AVX-512. README:40-41's 'GPU effect' is therefore really a hardware-platform effect. 'Shared seeds give no pairing' is true, but the README does not claim pairing; it claims a balanced comparison, which holds. (b) The A40 pool is mid-upgrade: cn-s-2, cn-s-4 and cn-t-1 are on 5.14.0-687.44.1.el9_8, the rest on 611.55.1.el9_7. The A40 block will therefore probably run on mixed stacks, and episode() parses only the GPU name. The raw rollout.log keeps the Driver Version, and status.json keeps slurm_job_id, which sacct can map to NodeList, so provenance can be recovered. It just is not reported.
verdicts.fix_after: Reword README:40-41 and protocol.why_two_blocks to 'the two blocks compare hardware platforms (GPU model and its node pool) on the same rows and seeds; an unpaired, balanced comparison'. In episode(), parse 'Driver Version' from the rollout.log device table, and report per-block counts of (driver, host) in block_results, so the report can show that the stack did not matter. Cite the v5-v8 prefix evidence in the report rather than softening the GPU attribution.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. pose_index() returns development_pose_slot (8 rows). On v8's H10 data, the v9 'pose_stratified' function gives 0.0122, which is v8's 'by row p = 0.012'. The true cluster-stratified test (P_A/P_B/P_C via cluster_of) gives 0.0111, v8's 'by pose 0.011'. These are different tests under the same name. The misnomer also appears in compute(): analysis.py:361-367 keys strata by rid[3:5] (row slot) and names the field block_x_pose_stratified_exact_p. The manifest's secondary_reported_not_gated[0] and [2] inherit it, and so do driver.record_block (driver.py:370) and the per_pose_diff key.
verdicts.fix_after: Rename pose_stratified_exact_p to row_stratified_exact_p, pose_sign_flip_p to row_sign_flip_p, per_pose_diff to per_row_diff and block_x_pose_stratified_exact_p to block_x_row_stratified_exact_p, in analysis.py, driver.py:370, the README and manifest secondary_reported_not_gated. Optionally add a cluster-stratified exact test using cluster_of(). A 3-unit cluster sign-flip bottoms out at p=0.125, so it should not be offered.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. driver.read_result (driver.py:265-276) treats any status other than 'completed' as retry-eligible. run_matched_task.py:265-283 sets infrastructure_error on validate_result failures ('non-finite simulator state', checker/terminal disagreement, parameter mismatch) even though rollout.json exists. The README's 'no completed rollout' fits the code only if 'completed' is read as the status state, and the manifest stop_rule has the same ambiguity. There is a sharper consequence than the reviewer gave: a policy-caused validation failure that recurs on the single retry is never counted as a failure. It makes the block incomplete, and the block is then excluded from the classification altogether. Historically the risk is low: 256/256 v5-v8 dev benchmark status.json files read 'completed', and no v5-v8 campaign has an attempts/ directory.
verdicts.fix_after: List in the protocol exactly which states trigger a retry. Record every retried directory with its state and error in block_results. Pick one of two options: treat 'non-finite simulator state' as a policy outcome (counted as not settled and flagged, and not able to make the block incomplete), or declare now that a repeated validation failure voids the block, and say why.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed in code. In analysis.py:245-248 and 268, cs/cn/bs/bn and Fisher count every valid episode per arm, while the strata, diffs and McNemar (lines 243-259) use only rows where both arms are valid. The two sets differ only in incomplete blocks, which are already descriptive. The secondary p-values carry no multiplicity statement. This is close to cosmetic.

findings.title: The block deadline is checked only when a tick runs; a block that finishes after the deadline is recorded as complete
findings.evidence: past_deadline() is called only inside block_stage, at tick time. When a block has no live stage, it is marked 'done' as soon as every destination has status=completed and rollout.json. Neither read_result nor analysis.py compares the task's completed_utc (run_matched_task.py writes it around line 285) with protocol.block_deadline_utc. Ticks fire either when a waited array ends (the chain tick) or every 2 h (the watchdog). So an array that ends between the deadline and the next tick fires a chain tick that sees live=[] and bad=[] and returns 'done'. The matched arrays carry no Slurm --deadline, so Slurm does not enforce the deadline either. Tick latency makes this worse right now: `sbatch --test-only` of tick.sbatch in `share` estimates a start at 2026-09-30T11:50 PDT (18:50Z), about 33 h away. Historically the 66 v3-v8 ticks waited a median of about 1 s and at most 44 s. `--deadline=now+596648` and `--deadline=2026-10-05T17:00:00` both pass --test-only on the matched array (testonly_extra.txt).
findings.failure_scenario: The a40 block, delayed by drained nodes, starts late and its last task finishes at 2026-10-06T01:10Z. Its chain tick fires, or it fires late because `share` is starved. block_stage finds all 96 results and returns 'done', record_block stores complete=True, and the block enters the preregistered classification. The rule says that block is 'incomplete' and must be excluded, so the classification can move from 'partially measured' to 'replicates on both' or 'on one model'.
findings.fix: (a) Append a Slurm-native deadline to the per-block sbatch args at driver.py:307, e.g. `extra = [f"--constraint={...}", f"--deadline={relative_begin(parse_utc(self.manifest['protocol']['block_deadline_utc']))}"]`, so it covers both the block array and the retry. Slurm then never starts a task that cannot end by the deadline. (b) In read_result, or in analysis.block_results, treat a rollout whose status.completed_utc is later than block_deadline_utc as invalid. (c) Note for the write-up: tasks that Slurm removes with state DEADLINE (from deadline minus 45 min onward) make the array look 'failed' before past_deadline() is true. The retry would then be submitted, but because it also carries --deadline it cannot start, and the next tick reports 'incomplete'. That matches the rule.

findings.title: Any sbatch failure inside an unattended tick crashes the driver before it reschedules the chain tick and the watchdog, so the campaign stalls silently
findings.where: /nfs/hpc/share/sanchej7/Humanoid_Lite/lehome-fold-repro/campaigns/20260928-fresh-seed-remeasure-v9/scripts/driver.py:102-108 (sbatch raises RuntimeError), 413-420 (tick: advance() then schedule_ticks(), no try/except), 323-333 (retry submitted from inside a tick)
findings.evidence: sbatch() raises RuntimeError on any non-zero exit. tick() calls self.advance() and only then self.update_status/self.schedule_ticks/self.save, with no exception handling. If the running tick is the watchdog or the chain tick, the exception means no successor chain or watchdog is ever submitted. The Lock is released, but nothing calls the driver again. The campaign runs unattended for up to 7 days through conditions that make a transient submission failure plausible. The controller was upgraded today: /apps/slurm/current moved to 25.11 at 09:23 PDT, and `scontrol show config` reports SLURM_VERSION=25.11.8 while the PATH clients are 25.05.9. The all-GPU maintenance reservation root_204 runs 2026-10-01 08:00-16:00 PDT (15:00-23:00Z). The a40 submission is also unproven (SC-3). The same pattern exists in v7 and v8, but those runs lasted hours, not days. Caveat: the first tick is run interactively, so a failure at launch would be seen.
findings.failure_scenario: The rtx8000 array ends and its chain tick tries to submit block:rtx8000.retry1 for two tasks that left no rollout. slurmctld briefly returns 'Socket timed out' or 'Slurm temporarily unable to accept job' during the maintenance, sbatch exits 1 and the tick dies. No chain tick or watchdog exists, so the a40 block's completion, the deadline cancellation and the final classification never happen until a person notices.
findings.fix: Wrap the advance step, e.g. `try: self.advance()` then `except Exception as exc: self.event(f"tick error: {exc!r}")`, then always run update_status/schedule_ticks/save. Inside schedule_ticks, retry each sbatch once after a short sleep. If the chain submit still fails, still try to submit the watchdog so a successor tick always exists.

findings.title: Throughput of the a40 block: a per-user cap of 2 GPUs on ampere, contended by the user's own older A40 jobs, on nodes whose return date is unknown

verdicts.reason: Confirmed in the code. past_deadline() is called only inside block_stage (driver.py:316, 323). When a block has no live stage and every destination has status=completed and rollout.json (driver.py:320-322), the block is marked 'done'. Nothing compares status.completed_utc (run_matched_task.py:250, 285) with protocol.block_deadline_utc: a grep for 'deadline' finds no hit in analysis.py or read_result. The block arrays carry only --constraint (driver.py:307). An array that ends after 2026-10-06T00:00Z, and before the next watchdog tick (every 2 h, plus queue latency), therefore fires a chain tick that returns 'done' with complete=True. The manifest's deadline_rule says that block is 'incomplete' and excluded, so the classification can move away from 'partially measured'. This is a misapplication of a preregistered rule, which puts it at major. It is bounded (at most about 2 h plus tick latency) and outcome-blind (driven by timestamps, never by results), so it is not a blocker. The proposed fix (a) is harmful as written. `sbatch --test-only --deadline=now+1800` on the 45-min matched job returns 'Requested time limit is invalid' (exit 1). job_mgr.c:6950-6955 (25.11.8, the running controller version) rejects at submit any job whose earliest_start + time_limit is after the deadline. A retry the driver submits in the last 45 min before the deadline would therefore be rejected, and sbatch() would raise inside an unattended tick (see SC-2). now+3600 and now+596648 are accepted.
verdicts.fix_after: Primary fix (b): decide completeness from on-disk timestamps. In analysis.episode(), also return status.get('completed_utc'). In block_results(), set valid=False, state='after_deadline' when completed_utc > manifest['protocol']['block_deadline_utc'] (the parse_utc format). 'complete' and classify() then follow the preregistered rule however late a tick runs. Optionally mirror the check in driver.read_result so the block stage reads 'incomplete' rather than 'done' with complete=False. Do not add --deadline as written. If a Slurm --deadline is wanted anyway, add it only while deadline - now > time_limit (45 min) plus a margin, skip the retry otherwise, and treat a rejected submission as 'incomplete', not as an exception. Then refreeze the manifest.

verdicts.reason: The defect is real, but the reviewer's failure scenario is wrong. sbatch() raises on a non-zero exit (driver.py:106-107), and tick() runs advance() before update_status/schedule_ticks/save with no try/except (413-420). But when the crashing tick is the chain tick, the watchdog submitted by the previous tick is still pending: schedule_ticks only resubmits the watchdog when it is not alive and never cancels it (447-454). That watchdog, with --begin=now+7200, re-runs advance() within about 2 h. So 'no chain tick or watchdog exists' is false for the rtx8000-retry case the reviewer describes. A stall needs the failure to recur at that watchdog. Alternatively, it needs a crash in a watchdog tick while no chain is pending. There is one real single-failure path. In a watchdog tick whose `waiting` differs from chain_deps (for example, it just submitted a retry), line 435 runs scancel(chain), then line 444 runs sbatch for the new chain before the watchdog check at 447. If that one sbatch fails, the old chain is gone, no new chain exists, and me == watchdog, so nothing follows. Two findings rule out a deterministic chain rejection. A dependency on a purged job is rejected only for afterok/afternotok, not afterany (job_scheduler.c:4132-4141). And the ?-afterany and --begin=now+7200 shapes pass --test-only under 25.11.8. The consequence is a delay until someone re-runs the tick: the arrays keep running and the data are intact. Because no --mail-type is set, the stall is silent. If it spans the deadline, it compounds SC-1, which fix (b) above neutralises.
verdicts.fix_after: Wrap advance(): `try: self.advance()`, then on `except Exception as exc`, record `self.event(f'tick error: {exc!r}')`. Always run update_status/schedule_ticks/save afterwards. In schedule_ticks, secure a successor before cancelling anything: submit the watchdog first when this tick is the watchdog (or it is not alive), and scancel the old chain only after the new chain sbatch succeeds. Retry each sbatch once after a short sleep, and never let a failed chain submission skip the watchdog submission. Optionally add --mail-type=FAIL to tick.sbatch.
